subject: Contract: MedSys Health - SLA remedies and termination triggers
messages:
From: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@medsyshealth.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: carlos.mendez@medsyshealth.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedSys SLA - requested remedies and termination rights

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the draft contract. Procurement and security ran the SLA section past our risk committee. A couple of asks came out that we need to put on the table before Legal signs off:

- Fee at risk / escrow: we want 10% of our committed monthly value placed in escrow and released after 60 days if no repeat P1 incident.
- Termination right: if we experience two P1 downtimes (>=5 min impacting production) within a 30-day window, we need a right to terminate for convenience and receive a pro-rated refund for pre-paid committed fees.
- Liquidated damages: an explicit alternative to termination — if Redwood refuses termination, we expect liquidated damages equal to two months of committed fees for each repeat SLA failure beyond the first.

I know these are material asks. Our rationale: as a healthcare SaaS, availability windows are patient-facing and the downstream risk is high. Escrow + termination or LDs gives our execs the contractual levers they need.

Attached is the redline showing the exact language we prefer (see MedSys_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf). Please route to contracts/legal and advise next steps and an expected timeline for a response.

Best,
Sofia Reyes

Sofia — thank you for the clear redlines and the context. Looping in Karthik (contracts) and Marissa (sales lead) to review. High level from product/CS: we understand the impact on MedSys operations and want to be reasonable, but need to preserve a balanced remedies model that doesn't create perverse availability incentives.

Initial thoughts (quick):
- We typically provide service credits as the primary SLA remedy rather than escrow or LDs.
- Termination for repeated P1s is an unusual step for Redwood; we prefer a staged remediation (root cause + 30-day cure window) before termination.
- If a customer insists on non-credit remedies, we need exec escalation and an underwriting review for a fee-at-risk construct.

Karthik — can Legal confirm whether the escrow / LD asks are feasible from Redwood's perspective and outline alternatives we can offer that satisfy MedSys' risk committee? Also advise on timeline — Sofia has indicated procurement needs an answer before their board meeting on 4/15.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedSys SLA - requested remedies and termination rights

Team — reviewed Sofia's redlines and the risk ask. Summary of constraints and negotiation posture: 

1) Escrow / fee-at-risk: Redwood is open to a limited fee-at-risk construct for strategic, regulated customers, but it needs to be tightly scoped. Proposed alternative: deposit equal to 10% of the first month's committed fee into a refundable hold for the first 6 months only (not an on-going escrow), to be released unless there is a confirmed repeat SLA violation. Full escrow of recurring monthly revenue is a non-starter.

2) Termination triggers: we cannot agree to immediate termination after two P1s in 30 days. Suggestion: allow termination only after (a) two P1s in 30 days AND failure to cure within a 30-day remediation period, OR (b) three P1s in 90 days. That gives engineering time to remediate and avoids spur-of-the-moment exits.

3) Liquidated damages: we can accept an LD cap as an alternative to termination, but it must be defined and capped. Proposed cap: one month's committed fee per qualifying SLA breach, up to a maximum of two months' fees in any 12-month period. Also include a reasonableness clause and exclusion for force majeure and customer's misuse.

4) Governance and telemetry: require joint incident reviews and a small set of predefined telemetry exports (no raw PHI) to validate downtime and assign severity. Security can approve a safe export mechanism.

Next steps: propose we send Sofia a clean counterproposal with those points and request an expedited executive approval path if MedSys insists on broader LD/termination language. I can draft the legal language today if you want.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@medsyshealth.com>

Evelyn / Karthik — thank you for the quick response and proposed alternatives. A few clarifications from procurement and legal at our side after internal review: 

- The temporary 6-month hold on first-month fees is better than nothing, but our board expects an ongoing economic deterrent. Can Redwood meet us halfway with a rolling 6% fee-at-risk retained each month (released after 45 days if no repeat incident)?
- The cure window language is concerning to our ops team — for patient-impacting outages we need the option to stop taking risk quickly. Can we shorten the cure period to 15 days for repeat P1 incidents?
- For LDs, MedSys can accept a cap but needs it to be at least equal to one month's committed fees per qualifying event. We cannot accept a cap lower than that.

We don't want to escalate to execs prematurely — our preference is to find final redline language this week. We can make an exceptions committee available if Redwood needs a one-off approval. Also attaching a brief incident log for the March outage that framed urgency for the board (Incident_Report_20270402.csv).

Sofia

Attachment: Incident_Report_20270402.csv (CSV, 18KB)

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedSys SLA - requested remedies and termination rights

Sofia — appreciate the specificity and the incident log. We want to be pragmatic and avoid delaying your board. Proposed compromise below — if MedSys can accept this, I'll escalate for one-off executive sign-off today and send a redline: 

1) Rolling fee-at-risk: Redwood will hold 6% of each monthly committed fee for the life of the initial 12-month term. Each monthly hold will be released after 45 days if no repeat P1 incident affecting that month's usage occurs. (This addresses the ongoing deterrent ask.)

2) Cure window: for repeat P1s, we'll allow termination after two qualifying P1s within 30 days only if Redwood fails to remediate within a 15-day cure period. (We can accept your shortened 15-day window for patient-impacting outages as you requested.)

3) Liquidated damages: if Redwood declines termination, LDs will be available at one month's committed fee per qualifying repeat event, capped at two months' committed fees in a 12-month period.

4) Confirmation/telemetry: we'll commit to joint incident reviews and a defined telemetry package (aggregated metrics only). Security will coordinate the export format.

If this looks acceptable, we'll circulate a final redline and request sign-off from Redwood's Head of Revenue and our General Counsel today. If you need any tweaks, call me and I'll join.

Best,
Evelyn
